ns2:course.label: Techniques for Engrg Decisions
ns2:course.description: Modeling of decisions in engineering work and the analysis of models to develop a systematic approach to making decisions. Fundamental concepts in linear and dynamic programming, probability theory, and statistics. Resource allocation, logistics, scheduling, sequential decision making, siting of facilities, investment decisions, application of financial derivatives, and other problems for decision making under uncertainty. Case studies from actual industrial applications illustrate real-world decisions. Prerequisite: ECE 210; credit or concurrent registration in ECE 313.
